title: keyframes context --json
description: What `keyframes context --json` writes: the plan's Principles, Constraints, Scenarios and Taste, each path given with the Map parts it meets, those parts, and the counts `check` would report. Items and parts are the report's items, under the same names. Within a schema_version, fields are only ever added, so a reader should ignore a field it doesn't know.

plan.description: The plan's name in the repo root, as the root spells it.

items.description: The items that print: Principles, Constraints, Scenarios and Taste, in that order, each section's items in line order.

paths.description: One entry for each path given, in the order given, a repeat listed once where it first appears. Empty with no paths.

parts.description: Every Map part some path meets, once, in Map order. Empty with no paths.

errors.description: The errors `check` would report on the plan.

warnings.description: The warnings `check` would report on the plan.

line.description: A line of the plan, counting from 1.

result.description: What a path or pointer resolved to; review is the review pointer, which a person checks.

path.description: A path in its usual form, its trailing / kept as given, and the IDs of the Map parts it meets, in Map order. A part meets a path when one of its paths is the same path, or one is inside the other, compared without a trailing /.

item.description: An item, with its ID, slug and keys in their usual form, whatever variant the plan used, and the sub-lines it has.

section.description: The section the ID's letter belongs to.

text.description: The item's prose without its ID or its sub-lines: its lines joined with a newline, their indentation removed.

paths.description: A Map part's paths, each in its usual form; a directory ends in /.

held_by.description: A Constraint's or Scenario's pointers, each in its usual form.

status.description: On Constraints and Scenarios: what their pointers add up to.

superseded_by.description: The decision that replaces this one, by its ID, or the value as written when it names none.

resolved_by.description: The decision that settled this question or idea, by its ID, or the value as written when it names none.
